mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 6.0% in a month, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown that triggers equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where both HOUST and INDPRO decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of active monetary tightening (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced corporate borrowing capacity.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past quarter signals strong consumer demand and economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST increases, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in CPI exceeds 3.5%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates a dual shock of labor market weakness and monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where both UNRATE and FEDFUNDS rise, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced corporate output and profit margins.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
